I added the option John asked about as version 311.0. It's published to the Marketplace, committed with only you as author, and pushed to master.

**What changed:** *⚙ → Settings... → Prompt* has a new checkbox under "Button only": **"Show the Send button in the toolbar instead of the prompt box"**. When it's on, the Send button goes back into the toolbar row just left of 📎, where it was before version 227.0. It's off by default, so nobody else's layout changes. It only affects the prompt box above the terminal. The native chat's own Send button stays where it is. The new text is translated into all 19 languages.

- **Tests:** all 1100 pass. I haven't tried it in Visual Studio (F5), so moving the button between the two spots and how it looks in the toolbar are untested.
- **Publish:** the usual first-try authentication error came up, the script's fallback publisher took over, and the upload succeeded.
- **Commit:** there's no Co-Authored-By line or model name. The commit tool in this repo did add an `Entire-Checkpoint: …` ID line on its own. It doesn't name an AI model, but tell me if you want it removed (that means rewriting the pushed commit).

**Email reply:**

---

Subject: Re: Send button location

Hi John,

Thank you so much for the kind words, I'm really glad the extension is useful to you!

You're right: in an earlier update the Send button moved into the corner of the prompt box. Your email made me realize some people prefer it with the other buttons, so I've just released version 311.0 with an option for that.

Once the update reaches you, go to **⚙ → Settings... → Prompt**. Under "Button only", tick **"Show the Send button in the toolbar instead of the prompt box"** and click OK. The Send button will go back to the toolbar next to the other buttons, the way it was before.

The Marketplace can take a little while to offer the update. If you don't see it yet, you can update manually from **Extensions → Manage Extensions → Updates**.

Thanks again for the feedback, and let me know if anything doesn't look right.

Best regards,
Daniel
